overall.summary: Every stated number reproduces (coverage, preservation, closed forms, 87 provenance-backed values, all 14 probe sweeps, every subgroup count, all 13 ablation AUCs, the linearisation). Nothing is refuted. Weakened: the open-two sweep (28% to above 99%) is a constructed empty-board case; on real positions the model goes 40% to 90%. The cell triggers named for units 2, 4, 6, 8 and 9 hold at the typical case but cover only 16% to 34% of each unit's active rows (unit9's "needs" rule 77%), and the four closed-form-only parts restate their formulas, as the record itself says.

unit1.why: The stored concept is a fitted sum of a count and four cells (score 0.67) and the hypothesis itself calls the unit "described by its formula rather than explained"; it is an offset that shrinks as x gains open twos, with cells carrying 81% of its weight.

unit2.why: It is on for 90% of positions with x at c3 (score 0.78) and lowers the score there as a correction, but two thirds of its active rows have c3 blank, so the cell rule is only part of its behaviour.

unit3.why: A centre-column reading the model confirms on real positions (acts on 81%, 98%, 100%, 100% of positions with 1 to 4 centre pieces, contribution rising +1.6 to +7.2), but 40% of its active rows have no x centre piece.

unit4.why: The x-at-g3 rule covers 72% of g3 positions but only a third of its active rows; its one clear game reading, firing on every x odd-row threat (+7.2 on 66 rows), is real but rests on too few rows.

unit5.why: A weak-position gate: on when x has no centre piece and few open twos (acts on 84.7% at zero open twos falling to 4.1% at five or more; 68.8% without a centre piece vs 31.4% with); -(centre_x + x_open_2) scores 0.63, a better match than the stored x_open_2 (0.53).

unit6.why: The x-at-c3 trigger accounts for 22% of its active rows and no concept reaches 0.5; it is a bottom-row cell pattern with no game reading.

unit7.why: It lowers the score less the more open twos x has (acts on 85% at zero to 30% at five or more, contribution -2.1 to -0.3), a consistent direction on real positions, but cells (e1, c3, e3, a4) set its level and the concept score is 0.33.

unit8.why: The o-at-c3 rule describes 16% of its active rows (it is on for 47% of x-at-c3 positions and 62% of blank-c3 ones); the growth with open ones is real but the unit has no reading that holds for most of where it acts.

unit9.why: The stated rule (x at c1 with o at b1, g1 or a1) scores 0.34: the unit is on for only 40% of positions satisfying it and 23% of its active rows do not.

unit10.why: It rises with x centre pieces and x at d2 on real positions (contribution -3.5 to -14.1 for 1 to 4 pieces, acting on 92% to 100%) and caps the centre column's positive effect; a compensating term with a partial centre reading.

direct_terms.why: A 58-term linear sum; the stated largest weights reproduce, but the part has no reading beyond its coefficients (concept score 0.08).

notes: Read-only: no database writes, no edits to the target directory; scratch files in the verify/ output directory only.
All evidence checked on the training split (n 54045).
The typical held case used by every probe sweep is an empty board with x_open_1 = 9, not an eight-ply position; directions were therefore confirmed on data subgroups as well.
